SMTO-HTTP-0039 — The service's sign-in address won't accept SMTO's request

GUID: aef60bf3-ae60-43e3-adfd-602acce64a19
Slug: http-auth-method-not-allowed
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO reached the sign-in address, but the service said it doesn't accept that type of request there. This points to a wrong sign-in address or setup, not a wrong password.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and check that Login path (or Token endpoint for OAuth) is the service's sign-in address, not an ordinary web page. SMTO submits sign-in details to that address, and pages meant only for viewing refuse submissions.
  2. Check the service's documentation for how sign-in works. If it uses a different kind of sign-in, change Authentication to match. A connection set up for the wrong kind of sign-in sends the wrong type of request.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. When it shows Authenticated, run the task again. This confirms the corrected setup works before the task uses it.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection, along with the service's documented sign-in method. Don't keep re-entering the password; it isn't the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The authentication endpoint returned HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed instead of a configured success status.

What this means

  • The authentication endpoint returned HTTP 405 instead of a configured success status. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The authentication endpoint returned HTTP 405 instead of a configured success status.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the configured exchange method with the endpoint's documented contract and routing.

How to fix it

  • Check the login or token endpoint and the method the profile uses (session logins built in the editor POST to login.path; OAuth token requests POST) against the target's API documentation, and correct the endpoint or auth type. A 405 does not indicate invalid credentials.
  • Correct the authentication HTTP method using authoritative API documentation. This response does not prove credentials are wrong.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The correct method reaches the intended login endpoint.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
